This article explains what data SPI needs and how to prepare them for the simple SPI (`spi_simple()`) or the model-based SPI (`spi_index()`).

## 1. What you need

The simple SPI uses annual NPAFP counts and annual population under 15. The model-based SPI uses monthly NPAFP counts, annual population under 15 and district boundaries.

The input requirements are:

| | Simple SPI, `spi_simple()` | Model-based SPI, `spi_index()` |
|---|---|---|
| NPAFP cases | One row per district and year | One row per district and month, including a zero count for months with no cases |
| Population under 15 | One row per district and year | One row per district and year |
| District boundaries | Not needed | Required, as an `sf` polygon layer with matching district identifiers |
| INLA | Not needed | Required |

## 2. Four things to get right

### Use the same district identifier in every table

Use a stable code, such as the POLIS district GUID (`adm2_guid`), rather than the district name. Spelling differences and name changes can prevent records from matching when tables are joined by name.

<details>
<summary>Check that the identifiers match</summary>


``` r
ids_cases <- unique(synth_surveillance$cases$adm2_guid)
ids_pop <- unique(synth_surveillance$population$adm2_guid)

# districts in the case data with no population
setdiff(ids_cases, ids_pop)
#> character(0)
```

The result is empty here, so every district identifier in the case data also appears in the population table.

</details>

### Keep districts and years with zero cases

**A missing row and zero cases are not necessarily the same thing.** If a district was under surveillance but reported no NPAFP cases in a year, retain that district-year with a zero count.

Supply a separate population table covering every district-year to be analysed. `spi_simple()` treats a district-year with a population record but no case row as zero reported cases. If you use one combined table, include a row with the population and a zero case count for each such district-year.

### Check the population

Population is used to calculate expected cases, so an abrupt change can affect the SPI. `spi_simple()` checks each district's population history. After calculating `spi_results` in section 3, use the following code to list districts flagged for review:


``` r
spi_results$population_qc |>
  dplyr::filter(population_qc != "ok")
```

A flag is a reason to check the population estimate, not to replace it automatically. A large change may reflect migration, displacement, a revised estimate or a district boundary change.

### Review changes in district geography

A new district may have no earlier records of its own. For a split or merged district, earlier records may cover a different area. Stable identifiers help with name changes, but they do not resolve changes in geography. Where possible, use a table linking old and new districts (a crosswalk) or prepare all years using the same district boundaries.

## 3. Data for the simple SPI

For the simple SPI, one table with one row per district and year is enough:

| district | year | npafp_cases | population_u15 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 2022 | 8 | 100 000 |
| A | 2023 | 10 | 105 000 |

The expected count uses the district's own rate over all earlier years. At least one earlier year and one earlier NPAFP case are needed for a positive expectation; otherwise SPI is `NA` and `history_check` explains why. Keep those district-years in the data so that zero reporting and missing history remain visible.

To try this with the bundled example data, create `afp_data` by adding the monthly counts for each district and year and joining the annual population:


``` r
afp_data <- synth_surveillance$cases |>
  dplyr::mutate(year = lubridate::year(month)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(npafp_cases = sum(count), .by = c(adm2_guid, year)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(synth_surveillance$population,
                   by = c("adm2_guid", "year")) |>
  dplyr::rename(district = adm2_guid, population_u15 = pop_u15)
```


``` r
spi_results <- spi_simple(afp_data)
#> ℹ Reading district-year counts...
#> ✔ 236 districts, 10 years (2015-2024).
#> ℹ Checking population series...
#> ✔ No unusual population pattern found.
#> ℹ Calculating expected cases for 7 assessment years (2018-2024)...
#> ✔ SPI calculated for 1644 district-years.
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Simple SPI summary ──
#> 
#> ── Formulas used
#> history_rate = preceding cases / preceding population x 100 000
#> expected = pop x history_rate / 100 000
#> oe = observed / expected
#> spi = oe / national_oe
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Data overview (2024)
#> Districts assessed: 236
#> Reported NPAFP cases (all districts): 6 085
#> National comparison (positive expected counts only): 6 085 reported; 4 771.9
#> expected
#> National observed/expected: 1.28
#> Districts with SPI below 1: 141 of 236
#> No SPI: 0 with no previous case, 0 with no previous year, 0 with no positive
#> national ratio
#> Population flags: 0
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Results by year
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

If the population is in a separate table, pass it as `population`:


``` r
afp_counts <- dplyr::select(afp_data, district, year, npafp_cases)
population <- dplyr::select(afp_data, district, year, population_u15)

spi_results <- spi_simple(
  afp_counts,
  population = population
)
#> ℹ Reading district-year counts...
#> ✔ 236 districts, 10 years (2015-2024).
#> ℹ Checking population series...
#> ✔ No unusual population pattern found.
#> ℹ Calculating expected cases for 7 assessment years (2018-2024)...

#> ── Simple SPI summary ──

#> expected = pop x history_rate / 100 000
#> oe = observed / expected
#> spi = oe / national_oe

#> 
#> ── Data overview (2024)
#> Districts assessed: 236
#> Reported NPAFP cases (all districts): 6 085
#> National comparison (positive expected counts only): 6 085 reported; 4 771.9
#> expected
#> National observed/expected: 1.28
#> Districts with SPI below 1: 141 of 236
#> No SPI: 0 with no previous case, 0 with no previous year, 0 with no positive
#> national ratio

#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 
#> ── Results by year
#> ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

If your columns have different names, specify them in the function call:


``` r
afp_custom <- afp_data |>
  dplyr::rename(adm2_guid = district, yr = year,
                npafp = npafp_cases, u15_pop = population_u15)

spi_results <- spi_simple(
  afp_custom,
  id_col = "adm2_guid",
  year_col = "yr",
  count_col = "npafp",
  pop_col = "u15_pop"
)
#> ℹ Reading district-year counts...
#> ✔ 236 districts, 10 years (2015-2024).
#> ℹ Checking population series...
#> ✔ No unusual population pattern found.
#> ℹ Calculating expected cases for 7 assessment years (2018-2024)...
#> ✔ SPI calculated for 1644 district-years.

#> ── Formulas used

#> expected = pop x history_rate / 100 000
```

<details>
<summary>Starting from monthly counts</summary>

Sum the monthly counts for each district and year before running `spi_simple()`. This example uses the package's synthetic data.

The complete population table supplied below restores district-years with no case rows as zero counts.


``` r
afp_harad <- synth_surveillance$cases |>
  dplyr::mutate(year = lubridate::year(month)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(count = sum(count), .by = c(adm2_guid, year))

res_harad <- spi_simple(
  afp_harad,
  population = synth_surveillance$population,
  id_col = "adm2_guid",
  count_col = "count",
  pop_col = "pop_u15",
  verbose = FALSE
)

res_harad
#> 
#> ── Simple SPI ──
#> 
#> Assessment years:   2018-2024
#> Districts:          236
#> Latest assessment:  2024
#> SPI < 1:            141 (60%)
#> SPI < 0.8:          93 (39%)
#> SPI < 0.6:          56 (24%)
#> Population flags:   0
#> No SPI:             0
#> Use summary() for the full report, as_tibble() for the table and
#> spi_simple_explain() for one district.
```

</details>

Use `spi_check_inputs()` with `method = "simple"` to check the table before calculating. It reports missing columns, duplicate district-years, invalid counts or populations, district-years with no row, and districts whose population series needs review:


``` r
spi_check_inputs(afp_data, method = "simple")
```

[Calculating the simple SPI](spi-simple.html) shows how the calculation works and how to inspect the result for one district.

## 4. Data for the model-based SPI

The model-based SPI needs monthly NPAFP counts, annual population under 15 and district boundaries. Use the same district identifier in all three inputs.

| district_id | month | count |
|---|---|---|
| A | 2022-01-01 | 1 |
| A | 2022-02-01 | 0 |

Include one row for every district-month, with a zero count for months with no cases. Start with all districts in the boundary file so that districts with no case records are included. Create a row for each district and month, then join the case counts:


``` r
boundaries <- synth_surveillance$boundaries |>
  dplyr::rename(district_id = adm2_guid)
monthly_counts <- synth_surveillance$cases |>
  dplyr::rename(district_id = adm2_guid)

# every district in the boundary file
districts <- tibble::tibble(
  district_id = unique(boundaries$district_id)
)

# every month in the period to analyse
months <- tibble::tibble(
  month = seq(min(monthly_counts$month), max(monthly_counts$month), by = "month")
)

# one row for every district and month
district_months <- dplyr::cross_join(districts, months)

# add the counts; a district-month with no count becomes zero
cases <- district_months |>
  dplyr::left_join(monthly_counts, by = c("district_id", "month")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(count = dplyr::coalesce(count, 0L))
```

Use `spi_check_inputs()` to check the case table, population table and district boundaries together. This check does not require INLA:


``` r
spi_check_inputs(
  cases = synth_surveillance$cases,
  population = synth_surveillance$population,
  shapefile = synth_surveillance$boundaries,
  id_col = "adm2_guid"
)
#> 
#> ── spi input check ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ✔ All input checks passed -- 236 districts x 120 months (2015-01 to 2024-12).
```

[Calculating the model-based SPI](spi-model.html) shows how to fit the model and calculate the SPI from these inputs.
